claims.text: Pre-exposure Q235 steel has an inherent thin passive iron-oxide film.
The naturally formed oxide film on Q235 steel is stable and continuous at room temperature in an aggressive NaCl-rich environment.
The naturally formed oxide film on Q235 steel is self-healing at room temperature.
A continuous oxide film impedes electrolyte attack and reduces corrosion.
At 700–900 °C, the oxide film on Q235 steel undergoes phase transformations.
Exposure at 700–900 °C generates cracks and spallation in the oxide film on Q235 steel.
High-temperature phase transformations and defect generation disrupt the continuity of the oxide film.
Disruption of the oxide film exposes the underlying Q235 steel to aggressive salt attack.
Exposure of the underlying steel following oxide-film failure accelerates corrosion.
At room temperature, Q235 steel will exhibit a low corrosion rate under the proposed NaCl-rich exposure.
At 700 °C and 900 °C, Q235 steel will show greater oxide-film phase change and defect formation than at room temperature.
At 700 °C and 900 °C, Q235 steel will exhibit greater mass loss or corrosion rate than at room temperature.
A reference steel with a robust high-temperature oxide film will outperform Q235 steel during high-temperature salt exposure.
Temperature can be isolated as the primary experimental variable by exposing otherwise identical Q235 samples at room temperature, 700 °C, and 900 °C in the same NaCl-rich environment.
Oxide-film integrity and phase composition, mass or weight change, and electrochemical impedance can be used as experimental observables for testing the proposed mechanism.
Applying an annealed HEA coating can alter corrosion resistance through formation of a protective oxide layer.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when Q235 steel has an additional protective coating or when salt chemistry is substantially changed.
The exact oxide phases and the temperature threshold for loss of film stability are unknown.

contradictions.description: The material is consistently introduced as pre-exposure Q235 steel, but the boundary field calls it 'pre-exposed Q235 steel,' which literally denotes a different exposure history and conflicts with the specified initial state.
